newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Zen-Noh says to cut Jan-Mar '97 feed price.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Zen-Noh says to cut Jan-Mar '97 feed price.

text.p: The National Federation of Agricultural Co-operative Associations said on Friday they would lower feed wholesale prices by 2,000 yen per tonne for the January-March 1997 period, against the October-December period of this year.

The federation, called Zen-Noh, is Japan's largest feed producer with about a 30 percent share of the domestic market. Other feed makers are likely to follow Zen-Noh's move, feed industry officials said.
The federation said in a statement that the price cut was due to the Chicago corn market's weakness since September.
The Chicago corn market had risen earlier this year, pushing up grain purchasing costs for Japanese makers. Corn is used here for making feed.
